grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: わたしはマイク・ミラーです。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしはマイク・ミラーです。` — I am Mike Miller.
**文型 2:** `サントスさんは学生じゃありません。` — Mr. Santos is not a student.
**文型 3:** `ミラーさんは会社員ですか。` — Is Mr. Miller a company employee?
**文型 4:** `サントスさんも会社員です。` — Mr. Santos is also a company employee.
**例文 1:** `［あなたは］マイク・ミラーさんですか。……はい、［わたしは］マイク・ミラーです。` — Are you Mr. Mike Miller? ...Yes, I am Mike Miller.
**例文 2:** `ミラーさんは学生ですか。……いいえ、［わたしは］学生じゃありません。` — Are you a student, Mr. Miller? ...No, I am not a student.
**例文 3:** `ワンさんは銀行員ですか。……いいえ、［ワンさんは］銀行員じゃありません。医者です。` — Is Mr. Wang a bank employee? ...No, he is not a bank employee. He is a doctor.
**例文 4:** `あの方はどなたですか。……ワットさんです。さくら大学の先生です。` — Who is that person? ...That is Mr. Watt. He is a professor at Sakura University.
**例文 5:** `グプタさんは会社員ですか。……はい、会社員です。カリナさんも会社員ですか。……いいえ、［カリナさんは］学生です。` — Is Mr. Gupta a company employee? ...Yes, he is. Is Ms. Karina also a company employee? ...No, she is a student.
**例文 6:** `テレーザちゃんは何歳ですか。……9歳です。` — How old is Teresa? ...She is 9 years old.

grammar.title: N1 は N2 です
grammar.explanation:
The particle は indicates that the noun before it (N1) is the topic of the sentence (see Topic and Subject article). The speaker forms a sentence by adding は to what he or she wants to talk about, and then makes statements about it.

Nouns used with です work as predicates. Besides indicating judgment or assertion, です also shows politeness towards the listener. です inflects when the sentence is negative (see 2. below) or in the past tense (see Lesson 12).
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしはマイク・ミラーです。` (I am Mike Miller.)
**例文 1:** `［あなたは］マイク・ミラーさんですか。……はい、［わたしは］マイク・ミラーです。` (Are you Mr. Mike Miller? ...Yes, I am Mike Miller.)
**1) Particle は**
**[Note] The particle は is read わ.**

grammar.title: N1 は N2 じゃ(では)ありません
grammar.pattern: N1 は N2 じゃ(では)ありません
grammar.explanation: じゃ（では）ありません is the negative form of です. じゃありません is often used in everyday conversation, while ではありません is used in formal speech and writing.
bulletPoints: **文型 2:** `サントスさんは学生じゃありません。` (Mr. Santos is not a student.)
**例文 2:** `ミラーさんは学生ですか。……いいえ、［わたしは］学生じゃありません。` (Mr. Miller, are you a student? ...No, I am not a student.)
**例文 3:** `ワンさんは銀行員ですか。……いいえ、［ワンさんは］銀行員じゃありません。医者です。` (Is Mr. Wang a bank employee? ...No, Mr. Wang is not a bank employee. He is a doctor.)
**[Note] The は in では is pronounced わ.**

grammar.linkedGrammarTitle: Noun か Noun か～ (Noun ka Noun ka～)

grammar.title: N1 は N2 ですか (Questions & Interrogatives)
grammar.pattern: N1 は N2 ですか
grammar.explanation:
The particle か is used to express uncertainty, doubt, etc. on the part of the speaker. A question can be formed simply by adding か to the end of a sentence. A question usually ends with a rising intonation.

This type of question is formed simply by adding か to the end of the statement, leaving the word order the same. The reply begins with はい if the statement is agreed with, and いいえ if it is disagreed with.

An interrogative replaces the part of the sentence that states what the speaker wants to ask about. The word order does not change, and か is added at the end.
bulletPoints: **文型 3:** `ミラーさんは会社員ですか。` (Is Mr. Miller a company employee?)
**例文 4:** `あの方はどなたですか。……ワットさんです。さくら大学の先生です。` (Who is that person? ...That is Mr. Watt. He is a teacher at Sakura University.)
**例文 6:** `テレーザちゃんは何歳ですか。……9歳です。` (How old is Teresa? ...She is 9 years old.)
**1) Particle か**
**2) Questions asking whether a statement is correct or not**
**3) Questions with interrogatives (だれ／どなた・何歳／おいくつ)**

grammar.title: N も
grammar.explanation: 「も」 is used when the same thing applies to a topic as was stated previously (replacing は).
bulletPoints: **文型 4:** `サントスさんも会社員です。` (Mr. Santos is also a company employee.)

**例文 5:** `グプタさんは会社員ですか。……はい、会社員です。カリナさんも会社員ですか。……いいえ、［カリナさんは］学生です。` (Is Mr. Gupta a company employee? ...Yes, he is a company employee. Is Ms. Karina also a company employee? ...No, Ms. Karina is a student.)

grammar.explanation: When a noun N1 modifies a following noun N2, の is used to connect the two nouns. In Lesson 1, N1 represents an organization or group to which N2 belongs.

grammar.title: ～さん・～ちゃん
grammar.explanation:
さん is added to the given name or family name of the listener or a third person to show the speaker's respect to that person. It should never be used with the speaker's own name. ちゃん is added to small children's names (such as テレーザちゃん or たろうちゃん) instead of さん to indicate familiarity.

When referring directly to the listener, the word あなた (you) is not generally used if the speaker knows the listener's name. The listener's family name followed by さん is usually used.
bulletPoints: **[Note] あなた is used to address someone with whom one is very familiar, such as one's spouse. Use the person's name + さん in normal conversation.**

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `これは辞書です。` — This is a dictionary.
**文型 2:** `それはわたしの傘です。` — That is my umbrella.
**文型 3:** `この本はわたしのです。` — This book is mine.
**例文 1:** `これはボールペンですか。……はい、そうです。` — Is this a ballpoint pen? ...Yes, it is.
**例文 2:** `それはノートですか。……いいえ、［これは］手帳です。` — Is that a notebook? ...No, this is a pocket notebook.
**例文 3:** `それは何ですか。……名刺です。` — What is that? ...It is a business card.
**例文 4:** `これは「9」ですか、「7」ですか。……「9」です。` — Is this a "9" or a "7"? ...It is a "9".
**例文 5:** `それは何の雑誌ですか。……コンピューターの雑誌です。` — What kind of magazine is that? ...It is a computer magazine.
**例文 6:** `あれはだれのかばんですか。……佐藤さんのかばんです。` — Whose bag is that over there? ...It is Ms. Sato's bag.
**例文 7:** `これはミラーさんのですか。……いいえ、わたしのじゃありません。` — Is this yours, Mr. Miller? ...No, it isn't mine.
**例文 8:** `このかぎはだれのですか。……わたしのです。` — Whose key is this? ...It is mine.

grammar.title: これ／それ／あれ
grammar.explanation: 2      これ , それ and あれ are demonstratives and work as nouns. これ refers to something near the speaker. それ refers to something near the listener. あれ refers to something distant from both the speaker and the listener.
bulletPoints: これ (kore): This thing near the speaker.
それ (sore): That thing near the listener.
あれ (are): That thing far from both speaker and listener.
どれ (dore): Which thing among three or more options?

grammar.explanation: この , その and あの modify nouns.
bulletPoints: Pattern: この / その / あの / どの + Noun.
Unlike これ/それ/あれ, these forms cannot stand alone and always require a noun.
Use どの when asking 'which [noun]?' among multiple items.

grammar.title: そうです
grammar.explanation:
In a noun sentence, the wordそう is often used to answer (in the affirmative) a question requiring an affirmative or negative answer. The expression はい、そうです can be used.

……はい、そうです。                            ……Yes, it is. そう is not usually used when answering a question in the negative; it is more common to say ちがいます (No, it isn't), followed by the correct answer.

……いいえ、違 います。                               ……No, it isn't.

……いいえ、ボールペンです。                             ……No, it's a ballpoint pen.
bulletPoints: ここ (koko): Here (near speaker).
そこ (soko): There (near listener).
あそこ (asoko): Over there (away from both).
どこ (doko): Where? (interrogative).

grammar.title: の substituting for a noun
grammar.explanation:
の can be used instead of a noun that has already been mentioned (e.g. instead of かば ん in example ⑪ ). If placed after the noun (as in example ⑪ , where it comes after the noun さとうさん), it enables N2(かばん)in N1 の N2(さとうさんの かばん) to be omitted. の is used as a replacement for things but not for people.

……佐 藤 さんのです。                                     ……It's Ms. Sato's.

……いいえ、わたしのじゃ ありません。                              ……No, it isn't [mine].

……はい、IMC の 社 員 です。                               ……Yes, he does. × はい、IMC のです。
bulletPoints: Pattern: Noun + じゃないです (is not Noun).
Formal alternative: Noun + じゃありません or ではございません.

grammar.title: お～
grammar.explanation: The prefix お is attached to words when the speaker is speaking politely (e.g.[お]  みやげ、[お]さけ)         .
bulletPoints: ね (ne): 'Isn't it?' / 'Right?' — seeks agreement or confirms shared knowledge.
よ (yo): 'I tell you!' / 'You know' — shares new information with certainty.

grammar.title: そうですか
grammar.explanation:
This expression is used by the speaker to acknowledge some new information he or she has just been given. It is pronounced with a falling intonation.

……いいえ、違 います。シュミットさんのです。 ……No, it isn't. It's Mr Schmidt's. そうですか。                  Oh, I see.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `ここは食堂です。` — This is the cafeteria.
**文型 2:** `エレベーターはあそこです。` — The elevator is over there.
**例文 1:** `ここは新大阪ですか。……はい、そうです。` — Is this Shin-Osaka? ...Yes, it is.
**例文 2:** `トイレはどこですか。……あそこです。` — Where is the restroom? ...It is over there.
**例文 3:** `山田さんはどこですか。……会議室です。` — Where is Mr. Yamada? ...He is in the meeting room.
**例文 4:** `事務所はどちらですか。……あちらです。` — Which way is the office? ...It is over there.
**例文 5:** `［お］国はどちらですか。……アメリカです。` — What country are you from? ...America.
**例文 6:** `それはどこの靴ですか。……イタリアの靴です。` — Where are those shoes from? ...They are Italian shoes.
**例文 7:** `この時計はいくらですか。……18,600円です。` — How much is this watch? ...It is 18,600 yen.

grammar.title: ここ／そこ／あそこ／こちら／そちら／あちら
grammar.pattern: ここ／そこ／あそこ／こちら／そちら／あちら
grammar.explanation:
The demonstratives ここ, そこ and あそこ refer to places. ここ indicates the place 3      where the speaker is, そこ the place where the listener is, and あそこ a place distant from both the speaker and the listener. こちら, そちら and あちら refer to direction and can also be used as politer-sounding alternatives for ここ, そこ and あそこ.

[ Note ] When the speaker regards the listener as sharing his/her territory, the place where they both are is designated by                                      あそこ ここ. In this situation, そこ indicates a place slightly distant from where they both are, and あそこ somewhere even further away.                                                                   そこ

grammar.title: どこ／どちら
grammar.explanation:
どこ is used for asking“Where?”and どちら for“Which direction?”どちら can also be used for asking“Where?”, in which case it is politer than どこ .

……あそこです。                               ……It's over there.

どこ and どちら are also used for asking the name of the country, company, school or other place or organisation to which someone belongs. なん cannot be used in this case. どちら is politer than どこ.

What company do you work for?

grammar.title: N1 の N2
grammar.explanation:
When N1 is the name of a country and N2 is the name of a product, it means that N2 is made in that country. When N1 is the name of a company and N2 is the name of a product, it means that N2 is made by that company. The interrogative どこ is used when asking where or by what company something is made.

What company is this computer made by? ……日 本 の コンピューターです。                             ……It's made in Japan. ……パワー電 気の コンピューターです。 ……It's made by Power Electric Company.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `今4時5分です。` — It is 4:05 now.
**文型 2:** `わたしは毎朝6時に起きます。` — I get up at 6 o'clock every morning.
**文型 3:** `わたしはきのう勉強しました。` — I studied yesterday.
**例文 1:** `今何時ですか。……2時10分です。ニューヨークは今何時ですか。……午前0時10分です。` — What time is it now? ...It is 2:10. What time is it in New York now? ...It is 12:10 a.m.
**例文 2:** `休みは何曜日ですか。……土曜日と日曜日です。` — What days of the week are your days off? ...Saturday and Sunday.
**例文 3:** `アップル銀行は何時から何時までですか。……9時から3時までです。` — From what time to what time is Apple Bank open? ...From 9 o'clock to 3 o'clock.
**例文 4:** `毎晩何時に寝ますか。……11時に寝ます。` — What time do you go to bed every night? ...I go to bed at 11 o'clock.
**例文 5:** `毎日何時から何時まで勉強しますか。……朝9時から午後3時まで勉強します。` — From what time to what time do you study every day? ...I study from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
**例文 6:** `土曜日働きますか。……いいえ、働きません。` — Do you work on Saturdays? ...No, I don't work.
**例文 7:** `きのう勉強しましたか。……いいえ、勉強しませんでした。` — Did you study yesterday? ...No, I didn't study.

grammar.title: 今 －時－分です
grammar.explanation:
To express time, the counter suffixes 時 (o'clock) and 分 (minutes) are placed after the numbers. 分 is read ふん after 2, 5, 7, or 9 and ぷん after 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10. 1, 6, 8 and 10 are read いっ, ろっ, はっ, and じゅっ(じっ)beforeぷん (see Appendix). 4       To ask the time, なん is placed in front of じ or ぷん.

……7 時 10 分です。                                      ……It's 7:10.

when a sentence expresses a behavior or event that will occur in the future. The table below shows its negative and past-tense forms. Non-past (future/present)                             Past Affirmative             おきます                                    おきました Negative               おきません                                   おきませんでした

changing the word order. When using an interrogative, this is placed in the part of the sentence that the speaker wants to ask about. When answering such questions, the verb in the question is repeated. そうです andちがいます(see Lesson 2)cannot be used when replying to a verb sentence question.

……はい、勉 強 しました。     ……Yes, I did [study]. ……いいえ、勉 強 しませんでした。 ……No, I didn't [study].

bulletPoints: **1) V ます works as a predicate. Using ます shows politeness toward the listener.**
**2) V ます is used when a sentence expresses something habitual or a truth. It is also used**
**3) Verb question sentences are formed by putting か at the end of the sentence, without**

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: わたしは京都へ行きます。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしは京都へ行きます。` — I go to Kyoto.
**文型 2:** `わたしはタクシーでうちへ帰ります。` — I go home by taxi.
**文型 3:** `わたしは家族と日本へ来ました。` — I came to Japan with my family.
**例文 1:** `あしたどこへ行きますか。……奈良へ行きます。` — Where are you going tomorrow? ...I am going to Nara.
**例文 2:** `日曜日どこへ行きましたか。……どこ［へ］も行きませんでした。` — Where did you go on Sunday? ...I didn't go anywhere.
**例文 3:** `何で東京へ行きますか。……新幹線で行きます。` — How are you going to Tokyo? ...I am going by Shinkansen.
**例文 4:** `だれと東京へ行きますか。……山田さんと行きます。` — Who are you going to Tokyo with? ...I am going with Mr. Yamada.
**例文 5:** `いつ日本へ来ましたか。……3月25日に来ました。` — When did you come to Japan? ...I came on March 25.
**例文 6:** `誕生日はいつですか。……6月13日です。` — When is your birthday? ...It is June 13.

へ 行きます／来ます／帰ります When a verb indicates movement to a certain place, the particle へ is put after the place noun to show the direction of the move.

5      [Note]The particle へ is read え .

grammar.title: N(vehicle)
grammar.explanation:
で 行きます／来ます／帰ります The particle で indicates a means or method. The speaker attaches it after a noun representing a vehicle and uses it together with a movement verb to indicate his or her means of transport.

When talking about walking somewhere, the speaker uses the expression あるいて. In this case, the particle で is not used.

grammar.title: いつ
grammar.explanation:
To ask about time, interrogatives using なん, such as なんじ, なんようび and なんが つなんにち are used. The interrogative いつ (when) is also used to ask when something will happen or happened. いつ does not take the particle に.

……3 月 25 日に 来ました。                         ……[I came ] on 25th March.

……来 週 行きます。                               ……[I'm going] next week.

grammar.title: ～よ
grammar.explanation:
The particle よ is placed at the end of a sentence. It is used to emphasise information which the listener does not know, or to show that the speaker is giving his or her judgement or views assertively.

Does this train go to Koshien?

There are a lot of horses in Hokkaido, you know. (See Lesson 18.) ⑯ マリアさん、この アイスクリーム、おいしいですよ。 Maria, this ice cream is very nice, you know. (See Lesson 19.)

grammar.title: そうですね
grammar.explanation: The expression そうですね is used to express sympathy or agreement with what the speaker has said. It is similar to the expression そうですか(see Lesson 2-8), but while そうですか is used by a speaker to acknowledge the receipt of some new information, そうですね is used to show sympathy or agreement with something the speaker already thought or knew. ⑰ あしたは 日 曜 日ですね。                            It's Sunday tomorrow, isn't it? ……あ、そうですね。                                ……Oh, yes, so it is.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: わたしは本を読みます。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしは本を読みます。` — I read a book.
**文型 2:** `わたしは駅で新聞を買います。` — I buy a newspaper at the station.
**文型 3:** `いっしょに神戸へ行きませんか。` — Won't you go to Kobe with me?
**文型 4:** `ちょっと休みましょう。` — Let's take a short break.
**例文 1:** `お酒を飲みますか。……いいえ、飲みません。` — Do you drink alcohol? ...No, I don't drink.
**例文 2:** `毎朝何を食べますか。……パンと卵を食べます。` — What do you eat every morning? ...I eat bread and eggs.
**例文 3:** `けさ何を食べましたか。……何も食べませんでした。` — What did you eat this morning? ...I didn't eat anything.
**例文 4:** `土曜日何をしましたか。……日本語を勉強しました。それから友達と映画を見ました。` — What did you do on Saturday? ...I studied Japanese. After that, I watched a movie with a friend.
**例文 5:** `どこでそのかばんを買いましたか。……メキシコで買いました。` — Where did you buy that bag? ...I bought it in Mexico.
**例文 6:** `あしたテニスをしませんか。……ええ、いいですね。` — Won't you play tennis tomorrow? ...Yes, that sounds nice.
**例文 7:** `あした10時に駅で会いましょう。……わかりました。` — Let's meet at the station at 10 o'clock tomorrow. ...Understood.

grammar.title: N を します
grammar.explanation:
A fairly wide range of nouns are used as the objects of the verbします, which means that the action denoted by the noun is performed. Some examples are shown below. 6    1)Play sports or games サッカーを します play soccer                  トランプを します play cards

パーティーを します give a party                   会 議を します hold a meeting

宿 題 を します do homework                 仕 事 を します work 電 話を します call, phone

44   3． 何を しますか This is a question to ask about someone's actions.

…… 京 都へ 行きます。                    ……I'm going to Kyoto.

……サッカーを しました。                        ……I played soccer.
bulletPoints: **2) Hold gatherings or events**
**3) Do something**

grammar.title: なん and なに
grammar.explanation:
Both なん and なに mean 'what'. なん is used in the following cases:

What do you say before going to bed? (See Lesson 21.)

なに is used in all other cases apart from 1) and 2).
bulletPoints: **1) When it precedes a word whose first sound is in the た , だ or な -row.**
**[Note]なんで is used for asking‘Why?’as well as‘How?' なにで can be used when** the speaker wants to make it clear that he or she is asking‘How?’
**2) When using it with a counter suffix.**

grammar.title: V ましょう
grammar.explanation:
This expression is used when a speaker is positively inviting the listener to do something with the speaker. It is also used when responding positively to an invitation. やす                                                                     45

……ええ、食べましょう。                          ……Yes, let's do that.
bulletPoints: **[Note]Vませんか and V ましょう are both used to invite someone to do something,** but Vませんか shows that the speaker is giving more consideration to what the listener might want than Vましょう.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: わたしはパソコンで映画を見ます。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしはパソコンで映画を見ます。` — I watch movies on my personal computer.
**文型 2:** `わたしは木村さんに花をあげます。` — I give flowers to Ms. Kimura.
**文型 3:** `わたしはカリナさんに（から）チョコレートをもらいました。` — I received chocolates from Ms. Karina.
**文型 4:** `わたしはもうメールを送りました。` — I have already sent the email.
**例文 1:** `テレビで日本語を勉強しましたか。……いいえ、ラジオで勉強しました。` — Did you study Japanese by TV? ...No, I studied by radio.
**例文 2:** `日本語でレポートを書きますか。……いいえ、英語で書きます。` — Will you write the report in Japanese? ...No, I will write it in English.
**例文 3:** `“Goodbye”は日本語で何ですか。……「さようなら」です。` — What is "Goodbye" in Japanese? ...It is "Sayounara".
**例文 4:** `だれに年賀状を書きますか。……先生と友達に書きます。` — Who do you write New Year's cards to? ...I write them to my teacher and friends.
**例文 5:** `それは何ですか。……手帳です。山田さんにもらいました。` — What is that? ...It is a pocket notebook. I received it from Mr. Yamada.
**例文 6:** `もう新幹線の切符を買いましたか。……はい、もう買いました。` — Have you bought the Shinkansen ticket already? ...Yes, I have already bought it.
**例文 7:** `もう昼ごはんを食べましたか。……いいえ、まだです。これから食べます。` — Have you eaten lunch already? ...No, not yet. I am going to eat now.

grammar.title: N1(person)
grammar.explanation:
に N2 を もらいます , etc. Verbs like もらいます, かります and ならいます indicate receiving things or information, so they are used with a noun indicating the person from whom those things or information are received. The particle に is used to denote that person.

I received some flowers from Mr. Yamada.

I borrowed a CD from Karina.

I'm learning Chinese from Mr. Wang.

I received some flowers from Mr. Yamada.

I borrowed some money from the bank.
bulletPoints: **[Note]から can be used instead of に in this sentence pattern. から is always used** when receiving something from an organisation such as a company or school rather than a person.

grammar.title: もう V ました
grammar.explanation:
もう means‘already' and is used with Vました. In this case, Vました means that the action has been completed. The answer to the question もう V ましたか as to whether an action has been completed or not is はい、もう Vました if in the affirmative (i.e. the action has been completed) and いいえ、Vて いません(see Lesson 31)or いいえ、まだです if in the negative (i.e. the action has not been completed). いいえ、Vませんでした is not used in this case, since this means that something was not done in the past, rather than that something has not been completed in the present.

[もう] 送 りました。 Have you sent the baggage yet? (See Lesson 31.) ……いいえ、まだです。                                    ……No, not yet.

examples.ja: もう荷物を送りましたか。 ……はい、 ……Yes,Ihave[sentit]. ……いいえ、まだ送っていません。

Particles are often omitted in informal speech when the relationships between the parts of speech before and after them are obvious.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `桜はきれいです。` — Cherry blossoms are beautiful.
**文型 2:** `富士山は高いです。` — Mt. Fuji is high.
**文型 3:** `桜はきれいな花です。` — Cherry blossoms are beautiful flowers.
**文型 4:** `富士山は高い山です。` — Mt. Fuji is a high mountain.
**例文 1:** `大阪はにぎやかですか。……はい、にぎやかです。` — Is Osaka lively? ...Yes, it is lively.
**例文 2:** `さくら大学は有名ですか。……いいえ、有名じゃありません。` — Is Sakura University famous? ...No, it is not famous.
**例文 3:** `ペキンは今寒いですか。……はい、とても寒いです。シャンハイも寒いですか。……いいえ、あまり寒くないです。` — Is Beijing cold now? ...Yes, it is very cold. Is Shanghai cold too? ...No, it is not very cold.
**例文 4:** `大学の寮はどうですか。……古いですが、便利です。` — How is the university dormitory? ...It is old, but convenient.
**例文 5:** `きのう松本さんのうちへ行きました。……どんなうちですか。きれいなうちです。そして、大きいうちです。` — Yesterday I went to Mr. Matsumoto's house. ...What kind of house is it? It is a beautiful house. And it is a big house.
**例文 6:** `きのうおもしろい映画を見ました。……何を見ましたか。「七人の侍」です。` — Yesterday I watched an interesting movie. ...What did you watch? "Seven Samurai."

grammar.title: Adjectives
grammar.explanation: Adjectives are used as predicates, and in sentences like Nは adj です they indicate the state of a noun or are used to modify a noun. They are divided into one of two groups, い -adjectives and な -adjectives, depending on how they inflect.

grammar.title: N は な -adj[な
grammar.explanation:
／]です N は い -adj(～い)です Adjective sentences that are non-past and affirmative end in です, which shows politeness toward the listener. Both types of adjective are attached to the front of です , but な -adjectives drop their な , while い -adjectives retain their(～い).

／] じゃ(では)ありません 8      The non-past negative of a な -adj is formed by dropping the な and attaching じゃ(で は)ありません to it.

The non-past negative of an い-adjective is formed by dropping the final い and attaching くないです to it.

な -adjectives                 い -adjectives Non-past affirmative   しんせつです                       たかいです Non-past negative     しんせつじゃ(では)ありません              たかくないです

sentences (see Lesson 1) and verb sentences (see Lesson 4). To answer such a question, the adjective is repeated. Expressions such as そうです or ちがいます cannot be used.

……いいえ、にぎやかじゃ ありません。 ……No, it isn't [busy].

grammar.title: ～が、～
grammar.explanation:
が connects two statements in an antithetical relationship. When these are adjective clauses with the same subject, if the initial clause remarks on the subject positively, the subsequent clause will remark on it negatively, and vice versa.

Japanese food is delicious, but it is expensive.

examples.audioKey: 日本の食べ物はおいしいですが、高いです。

grammar.title: とても／あまり
grammar.explanation:
とても and あまり are both adverbs of degree, and both come before the adjectives they modify. とても is used in affirmative sentences, and means 'very'. あまり, used with a negative, means 'not very'.

Beijing is very cold.

Sakura University is not a very well-known university.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: わたしはイタリア料理が好きです。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしはイタリア料理が好きです。` — I like Italian food.
**文型 2:** `わたしは日本語が少しわかります。` — I understand a little Japanese.
**文型 3:** `きょうは子どもの誕生日ですから、早く帰ります。` — Since today is my child's birthday, I am going home early.
**例文 1:** `お酒が好きですか。……いいえ、好きじゃありません。` — Do you like alcohol? ...No, I don't like it.
**例文 2:** `どんなスポーツが好きですか。……サッカーが好きです。` — What kind of sports do you like? ...I like soccer.
**例文 3:** `カリナさんは絵が上手ですか。……はい、［カリナさんは］とても上手です。` — Is Ms. Karina good at drawing? ...Yes, [Ms. Karina] is very good at it.
**例文 4:** `田中さんはインドネシア語がわかりますか。……いいえ、全然わかりません。` — Does Mr. Tanaka understand Indonesian? ...No, he doesn't understand it at all.
**例文 5:** `細かいお金がありますか。……いいえ、ありません。` — Do you have small change? ...No, I don't have any.
**例文 6:** `毎朝新聞を読みますか。……いいえ、時間がありませんから、読みません。` — Do you read the newspaper every morning? ...No, because I don't have time, I don't read it.
**例文 7:** `どうしてきのう早く帰りましたか。……用事がありましたから。` — Why did you go home early yesterday? ...Because I had an errand to run.

grammar.title: どんな N
grammar.explanation:
In addition to the responses explained in Lesson 8, a question sentence using どんな may be replied to by stating a specific name.

……サッカーが 好きです。                                      ……I like soccer.

9    3． よく／だいたい／たくさん／少し／あまり／全然

These adverbs are placed before verbs to modify them. Adverbs of degree            Adverbs of quantity 62      Used with an affirmative     よく   わかります                    たくさん あります Used with a negative        あまり わかりません                    あまり  ありません

That film is not at all interesting.
bulletPoints: **[Note]** すこし, ぜんぜん and あまり can also modify adjectives.

grammar.title: どうして
grammar.explanation:
The interrogative どうして is used to ask the reason for something. から is placed at the end of the reply giving the reason.

Why don't you read a newspaper in the mornings?                                       9 The question どうしてですか is used to ask the reason for something the other person has just said, instead of repeating what they said.

……どうしてですか。                               ……Why? 子どもの 誕 生 日ですから。                          Because it's my son's (daughter's) birthday.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: あそこにコンビニがあります。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `あそこにコンビニがあります。` — There is a convenience store over there.
**文型 2:** `ロビーに佐藤さんがいます。` — Ms. Sato is in the lobby.
**文型 3:** `東京ディズニーランドは千葉県にあります。` — Tokyo Disneyland is in Chiba Prefecture.
**文型 4:** `家族はニューヨークにいます。` — My family is in New York.
**例文 1:** `このビルにATMがありますか。……はい、2階にあります。` — Is there an ATM in this building? ...Yes, there is one on the 2nd floor.
**例文 2:** `あそこに男の人がいますね。あの人はだれですか。……IMCの松本さんです。` — There is a man over there, isn't there? Who is that person? ...He is Mr. Matsumoto from IMC.
**例文 3:** `庭にだれがいますか。……だれもいません。猫がいます。` — Who is in the garden? ...Nobody is there. There is a cat.
**例文 4:** `箱の中に何がありますか。……古い手紙や写真［など］があります。` — What is inside the box? ...There are old letters, photographs, and so on.
**例文 5:** `郵便局はどこにありますか。……駅の近くです。銀行の前にあります。` — Where is the post office? ...It is near the station. It is in front of the bank.
**例文 6:** `ミラーさんはどこにいますか。……会議室にいます。` — Where is Mr. Miller? ...He is in the conference room.

あります and います indicate the existence of a thing, person, etc. Since a sentence using these simply tells the listener that a thing or person exists, the noun representing that thing or person is marked by が .

**2) い ま す is used when what is present is animate and can move by itself, like people**

The noun is positioned at the head of the sentence and is marked with は . In this case, the noun must be something that both the speaker and the listener are aware of.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 会議室にテーブルが7つあります。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `会議室にテーブルが7つあります。` — There are seven tables in the conference room.
**文型 2:** `わたしは日本に1年います。` — I will stay in Japan for one year.
**例文 1:** `りんごをいくつ買いましたか。……4つ買いました。` — How many apples did you buy? ...I bought four.
**例文 2:** `80円の切手を5枚とはがきを2枚ください。……はい。全部で500円です。` — Please give me five 80-yen stamps and two postcards. ...Certainly. That is 500 yen in total.
**例文 3:** `富士大学に外国人の先生がいますか。……はい、3人います。みんなアメリカ人です。` — Are there any foreign teachers at Fuji University? ...Yes, there are three. They are all Americans.
**例文 4:** `兄弟は何人ですか。……4人です。姉が2人と兄が1人います。` — How many brothers and sisters are there in your family? ...There are four of us. I have two older sisters and one older brother.
**例文 5:** `1週間に何回テニスをしますか。……2回ぐらいします。` — How many times a week do you play tennis? ...I play about twice.
**例文 6:** `田中さんはどのくらいスペイン語を勉強しましたか。……3か月勉強しました。3か月だけですか。上手ですね。` — How long did Mr. Tanaka study Spanish? ...He studied for three months. Only three months? You are really good at it!
**例文 7:** `大阪から東京まで新幹線でどのくらいかかりますか。……2時間半かかります。` — How long does it take from Osaka to Tokyo by Shinkansen? ...It takes two and a half hours.

grammar.title: How to say numbers
grammar.explanation:
themselves are used when counting things from 11 and higher.

When counting people and things, various different counter suffixes are used depending on what is being counted. －人         People, except for one and two. One person is counted ひとり(1 人), and two people are counted ふたり(2 人). 4 人 is pronounced よにん . －台         machines and vehicles －枚         thin, flat things such as paper, shirts, dishes, and CDs －回         frequency, number of times －分         minutes －時 間       hours －日         days (This is the same as for dates, but 1 日 is pronounced いちにち, not ついたち.) －週 間       weeks 74           げつ －か月        months －年         years

11   2．How to use quantifiers

particle that determines the type of quantifier. However, this is not always the case with length of time.

I studied Japanese for two months in my home country.

(1)いくつ The word いくつ is used when asking how many there are of the items counted by the method explained in 1-1).

(2)なん＋ counter suffix なん＋ counter suffix is used when asking how many there are of things with a counter suffix attached as in 1-2).

How many foreign people are there in this company?

How many hours do you study Japanese every night? (3)どのくらい どのくらい is used to ask the length of time something takes.

How long did you study Japanese for?

How long does it take from Osaka to Tokyo?

ぐらい is added after quantifiers to mean 'about'. がっこう       せんせい            にん                                                             75

There are about thirty teachers at our school.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `きのうは雨でした。` — It was rainy yesterday.
**文型 2:** `きのうは寒かったです。` — It was cold yesterday.
**文型 3:** `北海道は九州より大きいです。` — Hokkaido is larger than Kyushu.
**文型 4:** `わたしは1年で夏がいちばん好きです。` — Of the whole year, I like summer the best.
**例文 1:** `京都は静かでしたか。……いいえ、静かじゃありませんでした。` — Was Kyoto quiet? ...No, it was not quiet.
**例文 2:** `旅行は楽しかったですか。……はい、楽しかったです。天気はよかったですか。……いいえ、あまりよくなかったです。` — Was the trip enjoyable? ...Yes, it was enjoyable. Was the weather good? ...No, it wasn't very good.
**例文 3:** `きのうのパーティーはどうでしたか。……とてもにぎやかでした。いろいろな人に会いました。` — How was yesterday's party? ...It was very lively. I met all kinds of people.
**例文 4:** `ニューヨークは大阪より寒いですか。……ええ、ずっと寒いです。` — Is New York colder than Osaka? ...Yes, it is much colder.
**例文 5:** `空港までバスと電車とどちらが速いですか。……電車のほうが速いです。` — Which is faster to the airport, the bus or the train? ...The train is faster.
**例文 6:** `海と山とどちらが好きですか。……どちらも好きです。` — Which do you like better, the sea or the mountains? ...I like both.
**例文 7:** `日本料理［の中］で何がいちばん好きですか。……てんぷらがいちばん好きです。` — Among Japanese dishes, what do you like the best? ...I like tempura the best.

grammar.title: 何
grammar.explanation:
N1[の 中]で      が いちばん adj ですか ……N2 が いちばん adj です で indicates a range. This question pattern is used to ask the listener to choose, from a group or category denoted by N1, a thing, place, person, time, etc. that exhibits to the highest degree the state or quality described by the adjective. The interrogative used is determined by the kind of category from which the choice is to be made.

[の 中 ]で 何 が いちばん おいしいですか。 Which of all the Japanese dishes is the most delicious?

What was your favorite place in Europe?

Who is the tallest in your family?

……2 月が いちばん 寒 いです。                         ……February is [the coldest]. [ Note ]The particle が is attached to the interrogative even in an interrogative sentence asking about the subject of an adjective sentence (see Lesson 10).

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: わたしは車が欲しいです。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしは車が欲しいです。` — I want a car.
**文型 2:** `わたしはすしを［が］食べたいです。` — I want to eat sushi.
**文型 3:** `わたしはフランスへ料理を習いに行きます。` — I am going to France to learn cooking.
**例文 1:** `今何がいちばん欲しいですか。……新しいケータイが欲しいです。` — What do you want the most right now? ...I want a new cell phone.
**例文 2:** `夏休みはどこへ行きたいですか。……沖縄へ行きたいです。` — Where do you want to go for your summer vacation? ...I want to go to Okinawa.
**例文 3:** `きょうは疲れましたから、何もしたくないです。……そうですね。きょうの会議は大変でしたね。` — Since I am tired today, I don't want to do anything. ...Indeed. Today's meeting was tough, wasn't it?
**例文 4:** `週末は何をしますか。……子どもと神戸へ船を見に行きます。` — What are you going to do this weekend? ...I am going to Kobe with my child to see the ships.
**例文 5:** `日本へ何の勉強に来ましたか。……美術の勉強に来ました。` — What did you come to Japan to study? ...I came to study fine arts.
**例文 6:** `冬休みはどこか行きましたか。……ええ。北海道へスキーに行きました。` — Did you go anywhere for your winter vacation? ...Yes. I went to Hokkaido to ski.

grammar.title: V ます -form たいです
grammar.pattern: V ます -form たいです
grammar.explanation:
The form a verb takes when used with ます(e.g. the かい of かいます)is called its ます -form.

The pattern Vます -form たいです is used to express the speaker ' s desire to do something. The object of ～たい can be marked either with the particle を or with the particle が . ～たい inflects in the same way as い -adjectives.

(が)

(が) ……靴 を 買いたいです。                                ……I want to buy some shoes. (が)

13        My stomach hurts, so I don't want to eat anything. (See Lesson 17.) [Note 1]ほしいです and たいです can only be used when talking about what the speaker or listener wants. They cannot be used to talk about what a third person wants. [Note 2]Neither ほしいですか nor V ます -form たいですか should be used when offering someone something or inviting them to do something. For example, コーヒー が ほしいですか or コーヒーが のみたいですか are not proper ways of asking someone if they would like a cup of coffee. In this case, an expression such as コー ヒーは いかがですか or コーヒーを のみませんか should be used.
bulletPoints: **1) V ます -form**
**2) V ます -form たいです**

grammar.title: V ます -form
grammar.explanation:
N(place)へ                    に 行きます／来ます／帰ります N The purposes of the actions いきます , きます and かえります are marked by に .

I'm going to Kobe to have some Indian food. When the verb before に is N します(e.g. かいものします or べんきょうします)or N を します(e.g. おはなみを します or つりを します), it is used in the form N に いきます／きます／かえります .

I'm going to see a festival in Kyoto tomorrow.
bulletPoints: **[Note]When a noun denoting an event such as a festival or concert comes before に ,** the purpose of the action is usually interpreted as being seeing the festival, listening to the concert, etc.

grammar.title: どこか／何か
grammar.explanation:
どこか means 'anywhere' or 'somewhere', and なにか means 'anything' or‘something'. The particle へ comes after どこか and the particle を after なにか, but either of these can be omitted.

Did you go anywhere for your winter holiday?

I'm thirsty; I'd like something to drink.
bulletPoints: **[Note]は can be added to a word expressing time in order to make it the topic of a** sentence.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: ちょっと待ってください。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `ちょっと待ってください。` — Please wait a moment.
**文型 2:** `荷物を持ちましょうか。` — Shall I carry your luggage?
**文型 3:** `ミラーさんは今電話をかけています。` — Mr. Miller is making a phone call right now.
**例文 1:** `ボールペンで名前を書いてください。……はい、わかりました。` — Please write your name with a ballpoint pen. ...Yes, understood.
**例文 2:** `すみませんが、この漢字の読み方を教えてください。……「じゅうしょ」ですよ。` — Excuse me, please tell me how to read this kanji. ...It is "juusho."
**例文 3:** `暑いですね。窓を開けましょうか。……すみません。お願いします。` — It is hot, isn't it? Shall I open the window? ...Thank you. Please do.
**例文 4:** `駅まで迎えに行きましょうか。……タクシーで行きますから、けっこうです。` — Shall I go meet you at the station? ...I'll go by taxi, so no thank you.
**例文 5:** `佐藤さんはどこですか。……今会議室で松本さんと話しています。じゃ、またあとで来ます。` — Where is Ms. Sato? ...She is talking with Mr. Matsumoto in the conference room right now. Well then, I'll come back again later.
**例文 6:** `雨が降っていますか。……いいえ、降っていません。` — Is it raining? ...No, it isn't raining.

grammar.title: Verb Groups
grammar.explanation:
Japanese verbs conjugate, and sentences with various meanings can be formed by adding various phrases to the conjugated forms of the verbs. Verbs are classified into three groups depending on how they are conjugated.

In all verbs of this group, the last sound of the ます -form is from the い -column of the syllabary chart, e.g. かきます(write), のみます(drink).

In most verbs of this group, the last sound of the ま す -form is from the え -column (e.g. たべます (eat) and みせます (show)), but in some verbs it is a sound from the い -column (e.g. みます (see)).

Verbs of this group include します and 'action-denoting noun ＋します ', as well as きます .
bulletPoints: **1) Group I Verbs**
**2) Group II verbs**
**3) Group III Verbs**

grammar.title: V て -form
grammar.explanation:
The verb form that ends with て or で is called the て -form. The method by which the て-form is created from the ます -form depends on the group to which the verb belongs, as described below. (See Exercise A1, Lesson14 of Main Text.) 92   1)Group I Verbs (1)When the last sound of the ます -form is い, ち or り, the い, ち or り is dropped and って is attached.       e.g. かいます → かって buy まちます → まって wait                     かえります → かえって go home, return (2)When the last sound of the ます -form is み, び or に , the み , び or に is dropped and んで is attached.       e.g. のみます → のんで drink よびます → よんで call                     しにます → しんで die (3)When the last sound of the ます -form is き or ぎ , the き or ぎ is dropped and い て or いで respectively is attached. 14         e.g. かきます → かいて write                   いそぎます → いそいで hurry However いきます (go) is an exception, and becomes いって . (4)When the last sound of the ます -form is し , て is added to the ます -form. e.g. かします → かして lend

て is added to the ます -form.        e.g. たべます → たべて eat みせます → みせて show                    みます → みて see

て is added to the ます -form.        e.g. きます → きて come します → して do                さんぽします → さんぽして go for a walk
bulletPoints: **2) Group II Verbs**
**3) Group III Verbs**

grammar.title: V て -form ください                Please do......
grammar.pattern: V て -form ください                Please do......
grammar.explanation:
This sentence pattern is used to tell, request or invite the listener to do something.

However, it is not a very polite way of asking someone to do something, so it is often used together with the expression すみませんが as in ① below.

Excuse me, could you tell me how to read this kanji, please? (Requesting)

Please write your name with a ballpoint pen. (Telling)

grammar.title: N が V
grammar.explanation: When describing a phenomenon by saying what was felt about it through one or more of the five senses (sight, hearing, etc.) or when telling someone objectively about an    14 event, the subject is marked with the particle が.

grammar.title: すみませんが
grammar.explanation:
Excuse me, could you pass the salt, please?

The が in expressions such as すみませんが and しつれいですが (used as introductory remarks when addressing someone) is not being used in an antithetical sense but as a casual preamble to a remark.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 写真を撮ってもいいですか。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `写真を撮ってもいいですか。` — May I take a photograph?
**文型 2:** `サントスさんは電子辞書を持っています。` — Mr. Santos has an electronic dictionary.
**例文 1:** `このカタログをもらってもいいですか。……ええ、いいですよ。どうぞ。` — May I have this catalog? ...Yes, you may. Go ahead.
**例文 2:** `この辞書を借りてもいいですか。……すみません、ちょっと……。今使っています。` — May I borrow this dictionary? ...I'm sorry, I'm afraid not... I am using it right now.
**例文 3:** `ここで遊んではいけません。……はい。` — You must not play here. ...Yes, ma'am.
**例文 4:** `市役所の電話番号を知っていますか。……いいえ、知りません。` — Do you know the phone number of City Hall? ...No, I don't know it.
**例文 5:** `マリアさんはどこに住んでいますか。……大阪に住んでいます。` — Where does Maria live? ...She lives in Osaka.
**例文 6:** `ワンさんは結婚していますか。……いいえ、独身です。` — Is Mr. Wang married? ...No, he is single.
**例文 7:** `お仕事は何ですか。……教師です。高校で教えています。` — What is your occupation? ...I am a teacher. I teach at a senior high school.

grammar.title: V て -form も いいですか                     May I do......?
grammar.pattern: V て -form も いいですか                     May I do......?
grammar.explanation:
This sentence pattern is used for asking permission to do something.

When withholding permission or stating that something is prohibited, an apologetic or euphemistic answer may be given, or the reason may be given, as illustrated in ② (with holding permission,) and ③ and 2 (stating that something is prohibited) below.

……すみません、ちょっと……。 のどが 痛 いですから。 ……Sorry, I'd prefer it if you didn't. I've got a sore throat. (See Lessson 17.)

……いいえ、[吸っては]いけません。 禁 煙 ですから。 ……No, it isn't. It's a No Smoking area.

grammar.title: V て -form います
grammar.explanation:
This sentence pattern is used in the ways illustrated below, in addition to expressing a continuing action as explained in Lesson 14.

15      ⑤ わたしは 結 婚 して います。                             I'm married.

[Note 1]The negative of しって います is しりません . Be careful not to say しって いません .

Do you know the number of City Hall? ……いいえ、知りません。                                 ……No, I don't.

[Note 2]The phrase もって います can mean either having something with you at the moment, or owning it.

personal status.

grammar.title: Nに V
grammar.explanation:
The particle に is used with verbs such as はいります, すわります, のります (ride; see Lesson 16), のぼります (climb, go up; see Lesson 19) and つきます (arrive; see Lesson 25) to indicate the location of the subject resulting from the action expressed by the verb.

⑯    京 都 駅 から 16 番の バスに 乗って ください。 Take the Number 16 bus from Kyoto Station. (See Lesson 16.)

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 朝ジョギングをして、シャワーを浴びて、会社へ行きます。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `朝ジョギングをして、シャワーを浴びて、会社へ行きます。` — In the morning I go jogging, take a shower, and go to the office.
**文型 2:** `コンサートが終わってから、レストランで食事しました。` — After the concert ended, I had a meal at a restaurant.
**文型 3:** `大阪は食べ物がおいしいです。` — Osaka has delicious food.
**文型 4:** `この部屋は広くて、明るいです。` — This room is spacious and bright.
**例文 1:** `きのう何をしましたか。……図書館へ行って、本を借りて、それから友達に会いました。` — What did you do yesterday? ...I went to the library, borrowed a book, and then met a friend.
**例文 2:** `大学までどうやって行きますか。……京都駅から16番のバスに乗って、大学前で降ります。` — How do you get to the university? ...I take the No. 16 bus from Kyoto Station and get off at Daigaku-mae.
**例文 3:** `今から大阪城を見学しますか。……いいえ。昼ごはんを食べてから、見学します。` — Are you going to tour Osaka Castle now? ...No. After having lunch, we will tour it.
**例文 4:** `マリアさんはどの人ですか。……あの髪が長い人です。` — Which person is Maria? ...She is that person with long hair.
**例文 5:** `太郎ちゃんの自転車はどれですか。……あの青くて、新しい自転車です。` — Which one is Taro's bicycle? ...It is that blue, new bicycle.
**例文 6:** `奈良はどんな町ですか。……静かで、きれいな町です。` — What kind of town is Nara? ...It is a quiet and beautiful town.
**例文 7:** `あの人はだれですか。……カリナさんです。インドネシア人で、富士大学の留学生です。` — Who is that person over there? ...She is Karina. She is Indonesian and an international student at Fuji University.

grammar.title: How to join two or more sentences together
grammar.pattern: How to join two or more sentences together
grammar.explanation:
Two or more sentences can be joined together using ～て(で).

When mentioning two or more actions that take place in succession, they are listed in their order of occurrence using the て -form. The tense of the sentence is determined by the tense form of the last verb in the sentence.

In the mornings, I go jogging, take a shower, and then go to work.

I went to Kobe, where I saw a movie and drank some tea.

おおき－い → おおき－くて                                  big ちいさ－い → ちいさ－くて                                  small い－い →             よ－くて(exception) good

／]→ ～で

104      ⑤ ミラーさんは ハンサムで、親 切 です。                                       Mr. Miller is handsome and kind.

grammar.linkedGrammarTitle: Verb てあげる (Verb te ageru)

grammar.title: V1 て -form から、V2
grammar.explanation:
In this sentence pattern, V2 expresses something done after V1. Because of this, V1 is often a precondition of doing V2 or an action preparatory to doing it. The tense of the sentence is determined by the tense of the last verb in the sentence.

Put the money in, please, and then press the button. The subject of V て -form から is marked with the particle が .

grammar.title: どうやって

grammar.title: どれ／どの N
grammar.explanation: どれ is an interrogative used when asking someone to specify one item out of a list of three or more . ⑰ ミラーさんの 傘 は どれですか。 Which is Mr. Miller's umbrella? ……あの 青 い 傘 です。                      ……It's that blue one. どれ cannot modify a noun directly. When modifying a noun, どの is used. ⑱ サントスさんは どの 人 ですか。 Which is Mr. Santos? ……あの 背が 高 くて、髪 が 黒 い 人 です。 くろ ひと                                                    16 ……That tall, black-haired man.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 写真を撮らないでください。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `写真を撮らないでください。` — Please do not take photographs.
**文型 2:** `パスポートを見せなければなりません。（見せないといけません）` — You must show your passport.
**文型 3:** `日曜日は早く起きなくてもいいです。` — On Sundays I do not have to get up early.
**例文 1:** `そこに車を止めないでください。……すみません。` — Please do not park your car there. ...I'm sorry.
**例文 2:** `もう12時ですよ。一人で大丈夫ですか。……ええ、心配しないでください。タクシーで帰りますから。` — It's already 12 o'clock! Will you be all right on your own? ...Yes, please don't worry. Because I will go home by taxi.

**例文 3:** `今晩飲みに行きませんか。……すみません。あしたからホンコンへ出張しなければなりません。ですから、早く帰ります。` — Won't you go for a drink tonight? ...I'm sorry. I have to go on a business trip to Hong Kong starting tomorrow. Therefore, I am going home early.
**例文 4:** `子どももお金を払わなければなりませんか。……いいえ、払わなくてもいいです。` — Do children have to pay too? ...No, they do not have to pay.
**例文 5:** `レポートはいつまでに出さなければなりませんか。……金曜日までに出してください。` — By when do we have to hand in the report? ...Please hand it in by Friday.

grammar.title: V ない -form
grammar.explanation:
The form of a verb that attaches to ない (e.g. かか in かかない ) is called its ない-form. The method by which the ない -form is created from the ます -form depends on the group to which the verb belongs, as explained below.(See Exercise A1, Lesson 17 of Main Text.)

The final sound of the ます -form of verbs in this group is always from the い -column, and this is changed to the corresponding syllable from the あ-column to make the ない -form. However, with verbs where the final sound is the vowel い(e.g. かいます and あいます)         , this changes not to あ but to わ. かき－ます → かか－ない                      いそぎ－ます → いそが－ない よみ－ます → よま－ない                      あそび－ます → あそば－ない とり－ます → とら－ない                         まち－ます →             また－ない すい－ます → すわ－ない                      はなし－ます → はなさ－ない

The ない -form of verbs in this group is the same as their ます -form. たべ－ます → たべ－ない み－ます →          み－ない

べんきょうし－ます → べんきょうし－ない し－ます        →                し－ない き－ます        →                こ－ない

grammar.title: Making an object the topic of a sentence
grammar.pattern: Making an object the topic of a sentence
grammar.explanation:
When making a noun in the expression N を V (i.e. a noun that is the direct object of a verb) into the topic of a sentence, the noun is placed at the beginning of the sentence and the particle を is replaced by the particle は . ここに           荷 物 を 置かないで ください。                    Don't put your bags here, please. 荷物を ＝は ここに 置かないで ください。

会 社の                 食 堂 で 昼 ごはんを 食べます。 I have lunch in the company cafeteria. 昼 ごはんを ＝は 会 社 の                     食 堂で    食べます。

I have lunch in the company cafeteria.

grammar.pattern: ミラーさんは漢字を読むことができます。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `ミラーさんは漢字を読むことができます。` — Mr. Miller can read kanji.
**文型 2:** `わたしの趣味は映画を見ることです。` — My hobby is watching movies.
**文型 3:** `寝るまえに、日記を書きます。` — Before going to bed, I write in my diary.
**例文 1:** `車の運転ができますか。……はい、できます。` — Can you drive a car? ...Yes, I can.
**例文 2:** `マリアさんは自転車に乗ることができますか。……いいえ、できません。` — Can Maria ride a bicycle? ...No, she cannot.
**例文 3:** `大阪城は何時まで見学ができますか。……5時までです。` — Until what time can we tour Osaka Castle? ...Until 5 o'clock.
**例文 4:** `カードで払うことができますか。……すみませんが、現金でお願いします。` — Can I pay by card? ...Excuse me, cash please.
**例文 5:** `趣味は何ですか。……古い時計を集めることです。` — What is your hobby? ...It is collecting old clocks and watches.
**例文 6:** `日本の子どもは学校に入るまえに、ひらがなを覚えなければなりませんか。……いいえ、覚えなくてもいいです。` — Must Japanese children memorize hiragana before entering school? ...No, they do not have to memorize it.
**例文 7:** `食事のまえに、この薬を飲んでください。……はい、わかりました。` — Please take this medicine before meals. ...Yes, understood.
**例文 8:** `いつ結婚しましたか。……3年まえに、結婚しました。` — When did you get married? ...I got married three years ago.

grammar.title: Dictionary form of verbs
grammar.explanation:
This is the basic form of a verb, as given in the dictionary. The method by which the dictionary form is created from the ます-form depends on which group the verb belongs to, as explained below.(See Exercise A1, Lesson 18, Main Textbook.)

With verbs in this group, the last sound of the ます -form, which is always in the い -column, is changed to a corresponding sound in the う -column. かき－ます          → かく            いそぎ－ます       → いそぐ よみ－ます          → よむ            あそび－ます       → あそぶ とり－ます          → とる             まち－ます       →  まつ すい－ます          → すう            はなし－ます       → はなす

る is added to the ます -form. たべ－ます          →    たべ－る み－ます          →     み－る

The dictionary form of します is する , while that of きます is くる .
bulletPoints: **1) Group I verbs**
**2) Group II verbs**
**3) Group III verbs**

grammar.title: N
grammar.explanation:
が できます          Can do...... V-dictionary form こと できます is a verb that indicates that a person has the ability to do something or that some behaviour is possible as a result of the situation. The object of できます is marked by が , and the ability or what is possible is expressed in the form of either a noun or the dictionary form of a verb with こと added to it.

Nouns indicating motion, such as(うんてん , かいもの , スキー and ダンス)can be used, as can nouns representing an ability, such as にほんご or ピアノ .

Mr. Miller can speak Japanese.

A lot of snow has fallen, so we can ski this year.

When a verb is used to describe an ability or possibility, こと is attached to the verb's dictionary form to make it a noun phrase, which is then followed by が できます .

(noun phrase)

(noun phrase)
bulletPoints: **1) In the case of a noun**
**2) In the case of a verb**

grammar.title: V1-dictionary form
grammar.explanation:
Nの                     まえに、V2                                     ......before...... Quantifier(time period)

This sentence pattern shows that V2 occurs before V1. Note that V1 always takes the dictionary form whether the tense of the sentence (i.e. the tense of V2) is past or non- past.

I studied Japanese before coming to Japan.

の is added after the noun. Nouns expressing motion can be used.

Note that の is not added to a quantifier (time period).
bulletPoints: **1) Verb**
**2) Noun**
**3) Quantifier(time period)**

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 相撲を見たことがあります。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `相撲を見たことがあります。` — I have seen sumo wrestling before.
**文型 2:** `休みの日はテニスをしたり、散歩に行ったりします。` — On days off I play tennis, go for walks, and so on.
**文型 3:** `これからだんだん暑くなります。` — From now on it will gradually get hotter.
**例文 1:** `北海道へ行ったことがありますか。……はい、一度あります。2年まえに、友達と行きました。` — Have you ever been to Hokkaido? ...Yes, once. I went with a friend two years ago.
**例文 2:** `馬に乗ったことがありますか。……いいえ、一度もありません。ぜひ乗りたいです。` — Have you ever ridden a horse? ...No, never even once. I would really love to ride one.
**例文 3:** `冬休みは何をしましたか。……京都のお寺や神社を見たり、友達とパーティーをしたりしました。` — What did you do during winter vacation? ...I visited temples and shrines in Kyoto, had parties with friends, and so on.
**例文 4:** `日本で何をしたいですか。……旅行したり、お茶を習ったりしたいです。` — What do you want to do in Japan? ...I want to travel, learn the tea ceremony, and so on.
**例文 5:** `体の調子はどうですか。……おかげさまでよくなりました。` — How is your physical condition? ...Thanks to you, I have gotten better.
**例文 6:** `日本語が上手になりましたね。……ありがとうございます。でも、まだまだです。` — Your Japanese has gotten very good, hasn't it? ...Thank you very much. But I still have a long way to go.
**例文 7:** `テレーザちゃんは何になりたいですか。……医者になりたいです。` — What does Teresa want to become? ...She wants to become a doctor.

grammar.title: V た -form
grammar.explanation: Forms of verbs ending in た or だ are called their た-form. A verb's た -form is created by changing the て or で of its て -form to た or だ respectively.(See Exercise A1, Lesson 19 of Main Text.) て -form → た -form かいて      → かいた のんで      → のんだ たべて      → たべた きて      →  きた して     →      した

grammar.title: V た -form ことが あります                      have the experience of V-ing
grammar.pattern: V た -form ことが あります                      have the experience of V-ing
grammar.explanation:
This sentence pattern is used to say what happened in the past as a particular experience.

Note that the past tense is used when simply mentioning something that happened in the past.

examples.en: I've ridden a horse.

grammar.title: V1 た -form り、V2 た -form り します                        V1, V2 and so on......
grammar.pattern: V1 た -form り、V2 た -form り します                        V1, V2 and so on......
grammar.explanation:
As already explained, the particle や is used when citing two or more nouns as typical examples from a longer list. This sentence pattern is used when doing the same with verbs. The tense is shown at the end of the sentence.

On Sundays, I play tennis, watch a film, and so on.

Last Sunday, I played tennis, watched a film and did some other stuff.

On Sunday, I played tennis and then watched a film. Unlike with this sentence pattern, V1 た -form り、V2 た -form り し ま す is used to enumerate a few typical actions from a longer list, indicating no time relationship between them. Because it is used to list actions non-exhaustively, it would be

19       unnatural to use it for mentioning actions that everyone usually does every day, such as getting up in the morning, eating meals, and going to bed at night.
bulletPoints: **[Note]Be sure not to confuse this sentence pattern with the V1 て -form、 [V2 て** -form、]V3 sentence pattern presented in Lesson 16, which is used to enumerate all the members of a list of two or more successive actions in their order of occurrence.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: サントスさんはパーティーに来なかった。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `サントスさんはパーティーに来なかった。` — Mr. Santos did not come to the party.
**文型 2:** `東京は人が多い。` — Tokyo has many people.
**文型 3:** `沖縄の海はきれいだった。` — The sea in Okinawa was beautiful.
**文型 4:** `きょうは僕の誕生日だ。` — Today is my birthday.
**例文 1:** `アイスクリーム［を］食べる？……うん、食べる。` — Want to eat some ice cream? ...Yeah, I'll eat some.
**例文 2:** `そこにはさみ［が］ある？……ううん、ない。` — Are there scissors over there? ...No, there aren't.
**例文 3:** `きのう木村さんに会った？……ううん、会わなかった。` — Did you see Ms. Kimura yesterday? ...No, I didn't see her.
**例文 4:** `そのカレー［は］おいしい？……うん、辛いけど、おいしい。` — Is that curry delicious? ...Yeah, it's spicy, but delicious.
**例文 5:** `あしたみんなで京都［へ］行かない？……うん、いいね。` — Won't we all go to Kyoto tomorrow? ...Yeah, sounds good.
**例文 6:** `何［を］食べたい？……今おなか［が］いっぱいだから、何も食べたくない。` — What do you want to eat? ...My stomach is full right now, so I don't want to eat anything.
**例文 7:** `今暇？……うん、暇。何？ちょっと手伝って。` — Are you free right now? ...Yeah, I'm free. What's up? Give me a hand for a moment.
**例文 8:** `辞書［を］持って［い］る？……ううん、持って［い］ない。` — Do you have a dictionary? ...No, I don't.

grammar.title: Polite style and plain style
grammar.explanation: The Japanese language has two styles of speech: polite style and plain style. Polite style                                Plain style あした 東 京 へ 行きます。                              あした 東 京 へ 行く。 I shall be going to Tokyo tomorrow.          I'm off to Tokyo tomorrow. 毎 日 忙 しいです。                                  毎 日 忙 しい。 I'm busy every day.                          I'm busy every day. 相撲が 好きです。                                    相撲が 好きだ。 I like sumo.                                 I like sumo. 富士 山 に 登 りたいです。                              富士 山 に 登 りたい。 I'd like to climb Mt Fuji.                   I want to climb Mt Fuji. ドイツへ 行った ことが ありません。                          ドイツへ 行った ことが ない。 I've never been to Germany.                  I've never been to Germany. The predicates used in polite-style sentences accompanied by です or ます are called the polite form, while the predicates used in plain-style sentences are called the plain form.(See Exercise A1, Lesson 20 of Main Text.)

grammar.title: Proper use of the polite style or plain style
grammar.pattern: Proper use of the polite style or plain style
grammar.explanation:
The polite style is used when speaking to a person one has met for the first time, to someone of higher status, and even to people in a similar age group whom one does not know very well. The plain style is used when talking to one's close friends, colleagues and family members. Be careful not to use the plain style to the wrong person, as this would be discourteous.

The polite style is commonly used in writing letters, while the plain style is used when writing dissertations, reports, diaries and so on.

**2) Writing**

grammar.title: Conversation in the plain style
grammar.explanation:
pronounced with a rising intonation instead, e.g. のむ( )or のんだ( ).

……うん、飲む。( )                            ……Yeah, sure.

the affirmative, ending the sentence with だ could sound a bit harsh, so it is either omitted entirely or replaced by a sentence-ending particle to soften the reply.

……うん、暇 ／暇 だ／暇 だよ。                    ……Yes, I am. (used by men) ……うん、暇 ／暇 よ／暇 だよ。                    ……Yes, I am. (used by women) ……ううん、暇 じゃ ない。                       ……No, I'm not.

evident from the context.

[を]食べる？                               Would you like something to eat?

[へ]行かない？                          How about going to Kyoto tomorrow?

[は]おいしいね。                          These apples are nice, aren't they?

However, particles likeで, に, から, まで and と are not omitted because the meaning of the sentence would be unclear without them.

……うん、持って[い]る。                     ……Yes, I have. ……ううん、持って[い]ない。 ……No, I haven't.

けど works in the same way as が and is often used in conversation.

[は]おいしい？    Is that curry good?

I've got some tickets for the sumo. Would you like to go with me? ……いいね。                               ……That'd be great.
bulletPoints: **1) Questions in the plain style usually omit the particle か from the end, being**
**2) In noun and な -adj questions, だ (the plain form of です ), is omitted. In an answer in**
**3) In the plain style, certain particles are often omitted if the meaning of the sentence is**
**4) In the plain style, the い of the V て -form いる is also often dropped.**

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: わたしはあした雨が降ると思います。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `わたしはあした雨が降ると思います。` — I think it will rain tomorrow.
**文型 2:** `わたしは父に留学したいと言いました。` — I told my father that I want to study abroad.
**文型 3:** `疲れたでしょう？` — You're tired, aren't you?
**例文 1:** `ミラーさんはどこですか。……たぶんもう帰ったと思います。` — Where is Mr. Miller? ...I think he has probably gone home already.
**例文 2:** `ミラーさんはこのニュースを知っていますか。……いいえ、知らないと思います。` — Does Mr. Miller know this news? ...No, I don't think he knows.
**例文 3:** `仕事と家族とどちらが大切ですか。……どちらも大切だと思います。` — Which is more important, work or family? ...I think both are important.
**例文 4:** `日本についてどう思いますか。……物価が高いと思います。` — What do you think about Japan? ...I think prices are high.
**例文 5:** `食事のまえに、お祈りをしますか。……いいえ、しませんが、「いただきます」と言います。` — Do you say a prayer before meals? ...No, I don't, but I say "Itadakimasu."

**例文 6:** `かぐや姫は「月へ帰らなければなりません」と言いました。そして、月へ帰りました。終わり。……終わり？お母さん、わたしも月へ行きたい。` — Princess Kaguya said, "I must return to the moon." And then she returned to the moon. The end. ...The end? Mom, I want to go to the moon, too.
**例文 7:** `会議で何か意見を言いましたか。……はい。むだなコピーが多いと言いました。` — Did you express any opinions at the meeting? ...Yes. I said that there are too many wasteful copies.
**例文 8:** `7月に京都でお祭りがあるでしょう？……ええ、あります。` — There's a festival in Kyoto in July, isn't there? ...Yes, there is.

grammar.title: Plain form と 思います                       I think that......
grammar.pattern: Plain form と 思います                       I think that......
grammar.explanation:
The ideas or judgements expressed with おもいますare indicated by the particle と. This sentence pattern is used in the following ways:

I think Teresa's already gone to bed. To express a negative conjecture, the clause before と is put in the negative.

Has Mr. Miller heard that news?

When asking someone ' s opinion about something, the expression ～に ついて どう おもいますか is used, without putting と after the どう.

134           ……きれいですが、ちょっと 交 通 が 不 便 だと 思 います。 What do you think of the new airport? Agreement with someone else's opinion is expressed like this:

……わたしも そう 思 います。                                 ……Yes, I think so, too.
bulletPoints: **1) When expressing conjecture**
**2) When stating an opinion**

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: これはミラーさんが作ったケーキです。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `これはミラーさんが作ったケーキです。` — This is a cake that Mr. Miller made.
**文型 2:** `あそこにいる人はミラーさんです。` — The person who is over there is Mr. Miller.
**文型 3:** `きのう習ったことばを忘れました。` — I forgot the words I learned yesterday.
**文型 4:** `買い物に行く時間がありません。` — I don't have time to go shopping.
**例文 1:** `これは万里の長城で撮った写真です。……そうですか。すごいですね。` — This is a photo I took at the Great Wall of China. ...Is that so? That's amazing!
**例文 2:** `カリナさんがかいた絵はどれですか。……あれです。あの海の絵です。` — Which is the picture that Karina painted? ...It's that one. That picture of the sea.
**例文 3:** `あの着物を着ている人はだれですか。……木村さんです。` — Who is that person wearing a kimono? ...It's Ms. Kimura.
**例文 4:** `山田さん、奥さんに初めて会った所はどこですか。……大阪城です。` — Mr. Yamada, where is the place you first met your wife? ...Osaka Castle.
**例文 5:** `木村さんと行ったコンサートはどうでしたか。……とてもよかったです。` — How was the concert you went to with Ms. Kimura? ...It was very good.
**例文 6:** `どうしましたか。……きのう買った傘をなくしました。` — What's the matter? ...I lost the umbrella I bought yesterday.
**例文 7:** `どんなうちが欲しいですか。……広い庭があるうちが欲しいです。` — What kind of house do you want? ...I want a house that has a large garden.
**例文 8:** `日曜日サッカーを見に行きませんか。……すみません。日曜日はちょっと友達に会う約束があります。` — Won't you go watch soccer on Sunday? ...I'm sorry. On Sunday I have plans to meet a friend.

grammar.title: Noun modification
grammar.explanation:
22       Lessons 2 and 8 explained how to modify nouns. ミラーさんの うち                                    Mr. Miller's house (See Lesson 2.) 新 しい うち                                      a new house (See Lesson 8.) きれいな うち                        a beautiful house (See Lesson 8.) The modifying word or clause comes before the noun. This lesson explains how to use a clause to modify a noun.

With な -adjectives, this is ～な, and with nouns it is ～の. 行く 人                           a person who goes to Kyoto きょう と        行かない 人                         a person who does not go to Kyoto

行った 人                          a person who went to Kyoto 行かなかった 人                       a person who did not go to Kyoto 背が 高 くて、髪 が 黒 い 人                           a tall, black-haired person 親 切 で、きれいな 人                                a beautiful, kind person 65 歳の 人                      a 65-year-old person 140   2)Noun-modifying clauses are used with the various sentence patterns illustrated below.

This is the house where Mr. Miller used to live.

The house where Mr. Miller used to live is old.

I bought the house where Mr. Miller used to live.

I like the house where Mr. Miller used to live.

There was a cat in the house where Mr. Miller used to live.

I've been to the house where Mr. Miller used to live.

This cake was baked by Mr. Miller.

I like the picture that Karina painted.

Do you know the place where he was born?
bulletPoints: **1) Verbs, adjectives and nouns in a clause that modifies a noun are in the plain form.**
**3) The subject of a noun-modifying clause is marked by が.**

grammar.title: V-dictionary form 時間／約束／用事
grammar.pattern: V-dictionary form 時間／約束／用事
grammar.explanation:
When talking about the time required for doing something or describing an appointment, errand, etc., the verb is put in the dictionary form and is placed in front of the noun じかん , やくそく, ようじ, etc.

I don't have time to eat breakfast.

I've arranged to see a film with some friends.

I have to do something at City Hall today.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 図書館で本を借りるとき、カードが要ります。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `図書館で本を借りるとき、カードが要ります。` — When you borrow books at the library, you need a card.
**文型 2:** `このボタンを押すと、お釣りが出ます。` — When you press this button, your change comes out.
**例文 1:** `よくテレビを見ますか。……そうですね。野球の試合があるとき、見ます。` — Do you watch TV often? ...Well, I watch it when there is a baseball game.
**例文 2:** `冷蔵庫に何もないとき、どうしますか。……近くのレストランへ食べに行きます。` — What do you do when there is nothing in the refrigerator? ...I go to a nearby restaurant to eat.
**例文 3:** `会議室を出るとき、エアコンを消しましたか。……はい、消しました。` — Did you turn off the air conditioner when you left the meeting room? ...Yes, I turned it off.
**例文 4:** `サントスさんはどこで服や靴を買いますか。……国へ帰ったとき、買います。日本のは小さいですから。` — Where do you buy clothes and shoes, Mr. Santos? ...I buy them when I go back to my country. Because Japanese ones are small.
**例文 5:** `それは何ですか。……「元気茶」です。体の調子が悪いとき、飲みます。` — What is that? ...It's "Genki-cha" [Health Tea]. I drink it when I'm not feeling well.
**例文 6:** `暇なとき、うちへ遊びに来ませんか。……ええ、ありがとうございます。` — When you are free, won't you come over to my house to visit? ...Yes, thank you.
**例文 7:** `学生のとき、アルバイトをしましたか。……ええ、時々しました。` — Did you work a part-time job when you were a student? ...Yes, I did sometimes.
**例文 8:** `お湯が出ません。……そこを押すと、出ますよ。` — Hot water isn't coming out. ...If you press there, it will come out.
**例文 9:** `すみません。市役所はどこですか。……この道をまっすぐ行くと、左にあります。古い建物です。` — Excuse me. Where is City Hall? ...If you go straight down this street, it is on the left. It's an old building.

grammar.title: V-dictionary form
grammar.explanation:
V ない -form ない い -adj(〜い)                   とき、〜(main clause)           When...... 23       な -adj な Nの とき is used to connects two sentences while expressing a time or occasion when the state or action described in the main sentence exists or occurs. The form of the word preceding とき is the same as the form that modifies a noun.

You need your card when you borrow a book from the library.

If you don't know how to use it, please ask me.

When I don't feel very well, I drink 'Genki-cha'.

Please come and visit me when you have some free time.

146          I take time off when my wife is ill.

I didn't study very much when I was young.

I often swam in the river when I was a child. The tense of the clause modifying とき is not affected by the tense of the main clause.

grammar.title: V-dictionary form
grammar.explanation:
とき、〜(main clause)           When...... V た -form When the verb in front of とき is in the dictionary form, whatever is described in the main clause happened before whatever is described in the ～とき clause. When the verb in front of とき is in the た -form, whatever is described in the main clause happened after whatever is described in the ～とき clause.

I bought a bag when going to Paris.

I bought a bag when I went to Paris.

way there, while ⑨ means that the bag was bought after arriving in Paris, i.e. it was bought in Paris.

grammar.title: V-dictionary form と、〜(main clause)                       If ...... then ......
grammar.pattern: V-dictionary form と、〜(main clause)                       If ...... then ......
grammar.explanation:
This sentence pattern is used to indicate that if a certain action, situation or phenomenon (the one before と ) occurs, then another action, situation or phenomenon (the one in the main clause, after と ) will inevitably occur.

If you press this button, you'll get your change.

When you turn this, it gets louder.

If you turn right, you'll see a post office.

items.prompt: 道をわたります・車に気をつけます
items.answer: 道をわたるとき、車に気をつけます。
items.hint: When crossing the street, I watch out for cars.

items.prompt: 使い方がわかりません・わたしに聞いてください
items.answer: 使い方がわからないとき、わたしに聞いてください。
items.hint: If you're not sure how to use it, please ask me.

items.prompt: うちへかえります・ケーキを買います
items.answer: うちへかえるとき、ケーキを買います。
items.hint: I buy a cake on my way home.

items.prompt: うちへかえりました・「ただいま」と言います
items.answer: うちへかえったとき、「ただいま」と言います。
items.hint: When I get home, I say, “I’m home.”

items.prompt: ねむいです・コーヒーを飲みます
items.answer: ねむいとき、コーヒーを飲みます。
items.hint: When I'm sleepy, I drink coffee.

items.prompt: ひまです・本を読みます
items.answer: ひまなとき、本を読みます。
items.hint: When I have free time, I read books.

items.prompt: 26さいです・結婚しました
items.answer: 26さいのとき、結婚しました。
items.hint: I got married when I was 26.

items.prompt: これをまわします・音が大きくなります
items.answer: これをまわすと、音が大きくなります。
items.hint: If you turn this, the volume will get louder.

items.prompt: ここをおします・お湯が出ます
items.answer: ここをおすと、お湯が出ます。
items.hint: Press here to get hot water.

items.prompt: 右へまがります・郵便局があります
items.answer: 右へまがると、郵便局があります。
items.hint: If you turn right, you’ll find the post office.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 佐藤さんはわたしにチョコレートをくれました。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `佐藤さんはわたしにチョコレートをくれました。` — Ms. Sato gave me chocolate.
**文型 2:** `わたしは山田さんにレポートを直してもらいました。` — I had Mr. Yamada correct my report.
**文型 3:** `母はわたしにセーターを送ってくれました。` — My mother sent me a sweater.
**文型 4:** `わたしは木村さんに本を貸してあげました。` — I lent a book to Ms. Kimura.
**例文 1:** `太郎君はおばあちゃんが好きですか。……はい、好きです。おばあちゃんはいつもお菓子をくれます。` — Taro, do you like your grandmother? ...Yes, I do. Grandma always gives me sweets.
**例文 2:** `おいしいワインですね。……ええ、佐藤さんがくれました。フランスのワインです。` — This is delicious wine, isn't it? ...Yes, Ms. Sato gave it to me. It's French wine.
**例文 3:** `ミラーさん、きのうのパーティーの料理は全部自分で作りましたか。……いいえ、ワンさんに手伝ってもらいました。` — Mr. Miller, did you make all the food for yesterday's party by yourself? ...No, I had Mr. Wang help me.
**例文 4:** `電車で行きましたか。……いいえ。山田さんが車で送ってくれました。` — Did you go by train? ...No. Mr. Yamada drove me there.
**例文 5:** `太郎君は母の日にお母さんに何をしてあげますか。……ピアノを弾いてあげます。` — Taro, what will you do for your mother on Mother's Day? ...I'll play the piano for her.

grammar.title: くれます
grammar.explanation:
The word あげます (give), which was taught in Lesson 7, cannot be used to talk about someone else giving something to the speaker or a member of his or her family. In that case, the word くれます is used.

I gave some flowers to Ms. Sato. ×佐 藤 さんは わたしに クリスマスカードを あげました。

Ms. Sato gave me a Christmas card.

Ms. Sato gave some candies to my younger sister.

grammar.title: あげます
grammar.explanation:
V て -form もらいます あげます, もらいます and くれます refer to the giving and receiving of things, while ～て あげます, ～て もらいます and ～て くれます are used to denote that an 152        action confers some kind of profit or benefit on the recipient.

The pattern verb て -form あげます is used when the person doing the action is taken as the subject. It shows that the action confers some kind of profit or benefit on the recipient.

I lent Ms. Kimura a book. Because the ～て あげます pattern denotes the conferral of some kind of profit or benefit, it could sound patronizing if used when the recipient is of higher status than the person conferring the profit or benefit. It is better in this case to use the pattern verb ます -form ましょうか(see Lesson 14-5).

Shall I call a cab? (See Lesson 14.)

May I help you? (See Lesson 14.)

Mr. Yamada told me the telephone number of the library. This shows that the speaker feels that the person for whom the action was performed (who is taken as the subject of this sentence) has received some profit or benefit from

the action. When the subject is わたし, it is usually omitted.

My mother sent me a sweater. Here, the person performing the action is taken as the subject, and the form shows that the speaker feels that the person for whom the action was performed has benefited from the action. When the person benefiting from the action (marked by the particle に) is わたし, it is usually omitted.
bulletPoints: **1) V て -form あげます**
**2) V て -form もらいます**
**3) Verb て -form くれます**

**[Note]In a sentence using ～て あげます or ～て くれます, the particle that marks** the person receiving the benefit is the same as in an equivalent sentence that does not use ～て あげます or ～て くれます . わたしに 旅 行 の 写 真 を 見せます。 ↓ わたしに 旅 行 の 写 真 を 見せて くれます。 He shows me the photos taken during the travel. わたしを 大 阪 城 へ 連れて 行きます。 ↓ わたしを 大 阪 城 へ 連れて 行って くれます。 He takes me to Osaka Castle. わたしの 引っ越しを 手伝います。 ↓ わたしの 引っ越しを 手伝って くれます。 He helps me move.

grammar.title: N1 は N2 が V
grammar.pattern: N1 は N2 が V
grammar.explanation: This wine is very nice, isn't it? ……Yes, Ms. Sato gave it to me. The response to this question takes as its topic the object of the sentence さとうさん が この ワインを くれました, i.e. この ワインを(see Lesson 17-5). Since こ の ワインは is understood by both the speaker and the listener, it can be omitted. As the subject of this sentence is さとうさん, it is marked by が.

grammar.title: 文型・例文 (Core Sentence Patterns & Example Q&As)
grammar.pattern: 雨が降ったら、出かけません。
grammar.explanation: Authentic core sentence patterns (文型) and contextual question-and-answer examples (例文) from the Minna no Nihongo I main textbook.
bulletPoints: **文型 1:** `雨が降ったら、出かけません。` — If it rains, I won't go out.
**文型 2:** `雨が降っても、出かけます。` — Even if it rains, I will go out.
**例文 1:** `もし1億円あったら、何をしたいですか。……学校を作りたいです。` — If you had 100 million yen, what would you want to do? ...I would want to build a school.
**例文 2:** `電車やバスが動かなかったら、どうしますか。……歩いて帰ります。` — What will you do if the trains and buses aren't running? ...I'll walk home.
**例文 3:** `あの新しい靴屋はいい靴がたくさんありますよ。……そうですか。安かったら、買いたいです。` — That new shoe store has lots of good shoes. ...Oh really? If they are cheap, I want to buy some.
**例文 4:** `あしたも来なければなりませんか。……無理だったら、来週来てください。` — Do I have to come tomorrow too? ...If it's impossible, please come next week.
**例文 5:** `もう子どもの名前を考えましたか。……ええ、男の子だったら、「ひかる」です。女の子だったら、「あや」です。` — Have you thought of a name for your child yet? ...Yes, if it's a boy, it's "Hikaru." If it's a girl, it's "Aya."
**例文 6:** `大学を出たら、すぐ働きますか。……いいえ、1年ぐらいいろいろな国を旅行したいです。` — Will you start working right after you graduate from university? ...No, I want to travel to various countries for about a year.
**例文 7:** `先生、このことばの意味がわかりません。……辞書を見ましたか。ええ。見ても、わかりません。` — Teacher, I don't understand the meaning of this word. ...Did you look in the dictionary? Yes. Even when I look, I don't understand it.
**例文 8:** `暑いとき、エアコンをつけますか。……いいえ、暑くても、つけません。体によくないと思います。` — When it's hot, do you turn on the air conditioner? ...No, even when it's hot, I don't turn it on. I think it's bad for your health.
